sections.title: Four down days, then a weak bounce

blocks.text: The IHSG fell 3.28% to 6,036.888 as foreign investors sold a net Rp5.04tn of shares, according to IDX. They were net sellers on all five days, and sold 59.6% more than the week before, when the figure was Rp3.16tn. The index fell four days in a row before gaining 27.386 points on Friday, and foreigners sold a net Rp1.27tn into that rise. The price steadied, but the selling did not stop.

blocks.label: 01 THE PRICE PATH
blocks.title: Four lower closes, then a small rebound

sections.title: Foreign selling on all five days

blocks.text: Wednesday was the heaviest day, with Rp1.61tn of net selling, or 32.0% of the week. IDX's weekly table puts the previous week's net selling at Rp3.16tn, so this week's Rp5.04tn was 59.6% more. Since the start of the year foreigners have sold a net Rp82.55tn, and this week alone was 6.1% of that.

blocks.label: 02 FOREIGN FLOW
blocks.title: Selling in every session, heaviest on Wednesday
blocks.note: Net foreign buying of shares each day, in Rp bn. IDX puts the weekly total at −5,036.31. The daily figures shown add up to −5,036.32, a Rp0.01bn difference in the published figures.

blocks.text: Who bought what foreigners sold

IDX's transaction table records whether the seller and the buyer in each trade were domestic or foreign. Foreign investors sold Rp14.19tn of shares to domestic buyers and bought Rp9.15tn from domestic sellers. The gap between the two is the Rp5.04tn net sale, and it matches the daily figures day by day. So domestic investors were the net buyers, with Rp39.99tn bought against Rp34.96tn sold. Foreign investors' share of trading value rose from 34% to 41%. But Rp13.98tn of the week's value, 22.1%, was trading between foreign accounts, which moves no money between foreign and domestic hands.

blocks.caption: Trading value by seller and buyer, 28 September to 2 October (Rp bn)

blocks.text: Wednesday stood out on both counts. Trades between foreign accounts reached Rp4.23tn, or 30.1% of that day's value, against about 20% on each of the other four days. The same day had the week's heaviest net selling. The table shows who traded, not why, so it cannot tell us whether these were block transfers or ordinary trades.

sections.title: Share volume jumped, trading value rose much less

blocks.text: Average daily volume rose 72.51% from the previous week, while average daily value rose 5.40%. Divide the week's trading value by the shares traded and you get Rp250.65 a share. On Friday GOTO alone traded 99,890 million shares, 82.77% of the day's volume, and Friday's 120,681 million shares were 47.9% of the week's total. Leave GOTO out and Friday's 20,791 million shares were fewer than any other day's total, while Friday's value of Rp12.25tn was close to the week's daily average.

Eight of IDX's ten biggest weekly losers, GOTO among them, started the week at Rp50 and ended between Rp24 and Rp33. IDX's statistics do not say why. Separately, trades in the negotiated market made up 13.83% of the week's trading value, or Rp8.73tn.

blocks.caption: Biggest weekly losers that started the week at Rp50

blocks.text: Of the 963 stocks in IDX's breakdown, 559 (58.0%) fell over the week and 224 (23.3%) rose. Stocks that fell more than 2% were worth Rp6,256tn, 59.2% of the total market value in that breakdown, against Rp2,482tn for the stocks that rose.

No sector index ended the week higher. Technology fell 12.45%, more than twice as much as the next worst, basic materials, at 5.29%. Energy held up best, down 0.99%. These returns show where the losses fell. They do not show who did the selling.

blocks.label: 03 WEEKLY SECTOR RETURNS
blocks.title: How each sector did
blocks.note: These are price changes in each sector index, not points added to or taken from the IHSG.

sections.title: GOTO took the largest share of the decline

blocks.text: IDX's index-mover table puts GOTO alone at 36.71 points of the IHSG's fall, 17.9% of the net 205.004-point drop, as its price fell 40% from Rp50 to Rp30. GOTO, AMMN and TLKM together took off 70.59 points, about a third of the net decline. The three biggest positive contributors, DSSA, UNTR and VKTR, added 16.37 points.

GOTO also helped Friday's rebound. It rose 7.14% that day and added 3.70 of the IHSG's 27.386-point gain, according to the 2 October daily report. Even so, it was still the biggest drag on the index for the week.
The largest actively traded shares

Flowless's 2 October snapshot puts these five stocks at the top by market value after screening for at least Rp50bn in average daily trading value over 20 sessions and no days without a trade. This describes size and trading depth. It does not say a share is a safe investment.

blocks.caption: Large, actively traded stocks at the 2 October close
headers: Estimated foreign net flow, 5 days, Rp bn

blocks.text: Four of the five, AMMN, TLKM, BBCA and BBRI, appear among IDX's ten biggest negative IHSG contributors this week. Flowless estimates each stock's foreign net flow from shares traded at the daily close, so the negative values in the table mean estimated net selling. They are not directly comparable with IDX's official market-wide foreign value. Flowless's average trading value also uses a stock-summary series that differs from the all-market totals in IDX Daily Statistics.

sections.title: A weak region, a weaker IHSG

blocks.text: Every ASEAN index in IDX's comparison fell, and the IHSG fell more than all of them except the Philippines' PSEi. Of the 32 other indices in the table, only four fell more, and four rose, led by Japan's Nikkei 225, up 2.93%, and Brazil's Ibovespa, up 2.03%.

The JISDOR rate eased 0.11% between the two Fridays, from 17,917 to 17,898. That slightly softened the loss for someone holding Indonesian shares in dollars without a currency hedge. During the week the rate moved between 17,877 on Wednesday and 17,998 on Tuesday. JISDOR is set at a different time from the stock market close, so this is a rough guide, not a return anyone could actually have locked in.

The latest rate decisions before the week were Bank Indonesia's hold of the BI-Rate at 5.75% on 23 September and the Federal Reserve's 0.25 percentage point increase on 16 September, which took its target range to 3.75% to 4.00%. Neither announcement points to a cause for this week's moves in shares.

blocks.title: The currency barely moved the result

sections.title: Watch the money, not the share count

blocks.label: Our stance
blocks.text: Stay defensive. Hold off on adding broad exposure until daily foreign selling eases and more than one sector recovers. Judge activity by trading value rather than share volume, which low-priced stocks pushed up this week. For investors holding in dollars without a hedge, the currency made little difference this week. The fall in share prices did the damage.
What would change our mind

First, a day when the index rises and foreigners are net buyers. This week had none, and Friday's gain came with Rp1.27tn of foreign net selling. Second, breadth. This week 434 stocks fell more than 2% and 144 rose more than 2%, and a recovery worth trusting would turn that around. Third, technology, the sector that fell most, steadying without one stock's volume carrying it. Fourth, daily trading value staying near this week's Rp12.6tn average while those signs appear.
These are things to watch, not forecasts. They are not tested support or resistance levels, and we do not put odds on them.

method: All returns are price returns. Rp bn means billions of rupiah and Rp tn means trillions. IDX marks trades as foreign or domestic using the domicile recorded in its trading system. That does not always tell us who ultimately owns the shares. The seller and buyer table adds up IDX's rounded daily figures, so its total of Rp63,127bn differs slightly from the exact weekly value of Rp63,125.87bn. Value per share traded is the week's trading value divided by the week's volume, both from IDX's trading summary. Breadth shares are worked out from IDX's counts. The dollar return based on JISDOR leaves out dividends, fees, taxes, hedging and tracking costs.
